Bound shell output is matched by protocol family and remote session ID. Buffered output keeps its order; failed local subscribers cannot terminate the shared peer.
LocalIpcShellForwardingTests; two concurrent bound commands in IntegrationTests.
Shutdown closes established connections before joining dialers. Each connection also observes lifetime cancellation, including late registration.
PeerSessionManagerTests: idle outbound lane and already-cancelled connection.
Filesystem errors carry structured codes. Native operations recover missing-path, access-denied, I/O and unsupported-operation exceptions; legacy text errors remain supported.
FileSystemTests: real protocol round trips and legacy decoding.

Input acquisition failures retry while retaining the monitor. Transient topology failures preserve ownership. Driver identities use the device name when hardware IDs are empty; asynchronous removal is confirmed before replacement.
HandoffLifecycleTests, WindowsTopologyTests and VirtualDisplayTests use fake hardware.
Stdin EOF closes the child input while the broker keeps watching for disconnect. Service cancellation and stream failures terminate the owned child process tree.
BrokerServerTests: EOF with open pipe, disconnect after EOF, and service cancellation.
Explicit mount intent survives automatic-mount settings and reconnects. Missing volumes or revoked access clear that intent.
RemoteMountManagerTests use fake adapters and cover setting changes, reconnects and disappearance.
Native flush/sync callbacks wait for fs.flush. Files flush to disk; Linux directories use fsync. Unsupported operations return errors instead of reporting success.
FileSystemTests and adapter tests; Linux directory flush exercised under WSL.
Binaries are staged and atomically replaced. Active daemons restart; inactive units are enabled and started. Failed installation or service operations return failure.
LinuxInstallerTests run with mocked systemctl: active/inactive units, failed restart/start, and failed staging.
Reloads reuse the browser session and CSRF token. Sessions expire and the store is bounded; opening another browser preserves existing sessions.
WebSessionTests cover reloads, independent browsers, expiry and eviction.
Bound close requests reach the remote command, local disconnect closes owned sessions, and completed commands release their session resources automatically.

Terminal input bypasses .NET's line reader through a duplicated file descriptor. Client input pumps run on the thread pool so synchronous terminal reads cannot block protocol setup. Size polling uses ioctl. One-shot commands stop stdin forwarding when the child exits, then drain stdout/stderr.
Linux ShellTests, blocking-input IPC integration, and a real PTY probe: exact input delivery without newline, no local echo, repeated size polling, and terminal restoration.
